data.content_ref: inline:The target's claim explicitly disavows justifying preference via likelihood or safety, yet its mechanism smuggles in exactly such a comparative judgment. The mechanism asserts that acting on a corroborated theory is justified because 'alternative untested theories are known to be even more risky (untested).' Calling untested theories 'even more risky' is a comparative risk/safety assessment — the very species of judgment the claim says it is abandoning. The target's own countercondition flags this ('If "best available" implies a comparative judgment of likelihood, induction creeps back in'), but the mechanism does not avoid that comparative judgment; it depends on it. Without the comparative claim that untested theories are riskier, the mechanism provides no reason to prefer corroborated theories over any untested rival, so the 'defensible' preference collapses into the inductive reasoning it claims to have abandoned.
